Topic 5.1: Listening and Speaking 5.1.1 Pronunciation And Vocabulary

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 5.1.1 Pronunciation And Vocabulary, part of Occupations Suggested vocabulary work, teacher, nurse, doctor, farmer, banker, s in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to face someone speaking to you?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 5.1.1 Pronunciation And Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: The learner’s ability to listen keenly and actively is enhanced as they listen to oral texts, recognise words with

the target letter-sound combinations and pronounce the words correctly.

• Digital literacy: The learner’s ability to create with technology is enhanced as they role play different occupations and records the videos.

Values:
Unity: Cooperation is enhanced as the learner collaborates with peers to develop a talking tree using vocabulary learnt.

37

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (Self-awareness): The learner’s self-awareness is nurtured as they learn about different occupations.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to apply the attentive listening skills in learning of other concepts in other learning areas.

Suggested Learning Resources

● Print textbooks in appropriate font size and colour contrast

● Braille books

● Digital devices with assistive technology,

● Charts, flash cards or braille cards,

● Pictures or picture description
